image.subject: Digory Kirke, a slim English boy of about eleven, short untidy brown hair, grey wool jacket and short trousers, kneels by a bed holding out a glowing golden apple to his mother, Mrs Kirke, a pale thin Edwardian woman in a white nightgown and shawl, lying in a bed, frail and weary

storyboard.claim: Digory gives the Narnian apple to his dying mother.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory kneels at the bedside offering the golden apple to his frail mother.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The apple from Narnia is now in his hands.
storyboard.addedInformation: The apple is the magic fruit, and the mother is the reason for it.

image.subject: Mrs Kirke, a pale thin Edwardian woman in a white nightgown and shawl, now sitting up in bed in bright morning sunlight, the curtains pulled back and a window thrown open to the summer air

storyboard.claim: The sickroom is opened up and the mother is restored.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mrs Kirke sits up in bed as sunlight floods in through an open window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The apple has done its work on his mother.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gloom of the sickroom has lifted.

image.subject: Digory Kirke, a slim English boy of about eleven, short untidy brown hair, grey wool jacket and short trousers, stands alone in a dusty attic study, a highback chair beside him, his empty hands held open at his sides

storyboard.claim: Digory saved his mother by giving up control of the power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory stands alone in the attic with empty open hands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The apple has healed his mother.
storyboard.addedInformation: He gave up control of the power he could not undo.

storyboard.claim: Digory refuses to exploit the world to fix his mistake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quote card stating that Digory refuses to exploit the world to fix it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: He gave up control of the power.
storyboard.addedInformation: The moral is stated in words, the picture would only repeat the attic.

image.subject: a red wooden tray on a dusty attic table holding the yellow and green magic rings, a ticking clock beside it in the gloom

storyboard.claim: A physical remnant of the adventure remains: the rings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The red tray with yellow and green rings on the attic table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The moral was stated, now the object.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rings are the one thing left to be dealt with.

storyboard.claim: What do the children do with the rings?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Question card asking what Digory and Polly do with the magic rings.
storyboard.onScreenText: NOT THE TRASH. NOT THE STUDY.
storyboard.addedInformation: They cannot be thrown away or left in Uncle Andrew's study.

image.subject: Digory Kirke, a slim English boy of about eleven, short untidy brown hair, sits alone at a kitchen table in the evening lamplight, eating the core of a golden apple

storyboard.claim: That evening Digory eats the core of the apple.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory eats the apple core alone at the table at night.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question about the rings was answered with a decision.
storyboard.addedInformation: The apple is eaten, its seed is left to be planted.

image.subject: a tiny silver-leaved sapling pushing up through dark damp London soil in a small backyard at dawn, a boy's muddy boot standing beside it

storyboard.claim: The next morning a small tree has grown from the buried core.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tiny silver sapling breaks through the soil at dawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Digory buried the core in the backyard.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tree is the young Narnian apple tree.

image.subject: Digory Kirke and Polly Plummer, a girl of about eleven, dark plaited hair, a long-sleeved cotton dress with a pinafore, kneel together in a muddy London backyard, a trowel between them, placing yellow and green rings into the soil

storyboard.claim: The children bury all the remaining rings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory and Polly kneel in the mud placing rings into the earth.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rings go into the ground along with the apple core.

image.subject: a small silver-leaved sapling standing in the centre of a tight circle of yellow and green rings half-buried in dark earth

storyboard.claim: The rings are buried in a circle around the tree, returning their power to the earth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sapling sits inside a ring of buried rings.
storyboard.addedInformation: The circle is around the base of the tree.

image.subject: Digory Kirke and Polly Plummer stand over the buried tree in a London backyard, both looking down at the ground with serious faces

storyboard.claim: The children look at what they have done and what the buried tree will do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two children look down at the planted tree.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rings are buried around the tree.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reader is asked to think about the tree's roots.

image.subject: a dark cross-section of London soil showing pale silver roots plunging down through the layers toward a ring of buried rings

storyboard.claim: The sapling's roots will plunge down to the buried rings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Silver roots reach down through the soil to the rings.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tree is planted over the rings.
storyboard.addedInformation: The roots reach the rings beneath the ground.

image.subject: a small pale grey heap of faintly glowing dust on dark soil under a dim lamp

storyboard.claim: The roots pass through a circle of dust that pulls matter into the wood.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Glowing dust in a ring with roots curling into it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The roots plunge down to the rings.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dust pulls matter into the wood between the worlds.

storyboard.claim: Decades pass and the tree survives every storm, full of magic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A timeline card marking the years while the tree stands through the storms.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tree has been planted and has rooted.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tree is infused with magic from the rings.

image.subject: Digory Kirke, now an old man with grey hair and a professor's tweed coat, stands beside a great tree blown down by a storm in a wrecked English garden, unable to bring himself to cut it

storyboard.claim: A storm blows the great tree down, and Digory, now a professor, cannot bear to chop it up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Old Digory looks at the fallen tree in a storm-wrecked garden.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Decades have passed and the tree has grown.
storyboard.addedInformation: The man is the same boy, grown old.

image.subject: a carpenter in a workshop, a tall half-built wardrobe of pale timber standing among wood shavings

storyboard.claim: The timber is harvested and a carpenter builds a wardrobe out of it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A carpenter works on a wardrobe made of the tree's timber.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tree has fallen and the old man cannot chop it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The wardrobe is built from the tree grown on the rings.

storyboard.claim: What happens when a little girl named Lucy opens the wardrobe door and steps inside?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Question card asking what happens when a girl named Lucy opens the wardrobe door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The wardrobe is built from the tree.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rings' pull reaches into the wardrobe.

image.subject: an old wooden wardrobe door standing slightly ajar in a dim room, pale golden light spilling out through the gap

storyboard.claim: The doorway was the harvest of a choice made by a grieving boy who decided not to steal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wardrobe door ajar with light spilling out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question was which girl opens the door.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door is the result of Digory refusing to steal.
